note: Synthesizes existing text/CDATA materialization experiments. It is not a new benchmark run and not a runtime-limit conclusion.

parserInput: Rows use StreamReaderSync over a synchronous Iterable<Uint8Array[]> generated by byteBatches(fixture).
arrayBufferConsumption: The corpus file is read once as a seed buffer and sliced into Uint8Array views; measured rows consume synchronous Iterable<Uint8Array[]> parser pulls, not a pure ReadableStream and not one full 1 GiB ArrayBuffer parser input.
batchBackpressure: byteBatches(fixture) yields one grouped Uint8Array[] batch per synchronous parser pull and does not prebuild the repeated 1 GiB+ stream.
readableStreamScope: This Node/Bun large matrix does not consume a pure ReadableStream directly; browser fetch streaming rows are measured in browser-candidate-headroom.

findings.summary: The fastest full-string text-materializing row remains 185.50 MiB/s, 14.50 MiB/s below the 200 MiB/s counterexample threshold.
4 near-full row(s) cross 200 MiB/s only after omitting text/CDATA strings.
evidence: text-trim-cost-decomposition.json: withoutText=249.13 MiB/s, full=185.50 MiB/s, omittedTextReads=16,987,392
text-trim-cost-decomposition-2gib.json: withoutText=243.31 MiB/s, full=184.92 MiB/s, omittedTextReads=33,974,712
text-trim-cost-decomposition-4gib.json: withoutText=252.36 MiB/s, full=178.86 MiB/s, omittedTextReads=67,949,424
text-trim-cost-decomposition-8gib.json: withoutText=237.38 MiB/s, full=184.03 MiB/s, omittedTextReads=135,898,776

findings.summary: Removing only text trim does not close the 200 MiB/s gap, and the fold-trim checksum variant is slower than the full row.
The current repeated text cache, bounded long-text cache, ASCII text fast paths, and fold-trim candidate rows do not reach the full target row.
Rows that omit text/CDATA strings identify headroom but are not full-string StAX counterexamples.
